artists.biography:
Nicholas Rodney "Nick" Drake (19 June 1948 - 25 November 1974) was an English singer-songwriter and musician who was known for his sombre guitar-based songs. He failed to find a wide audience during his lifetime but his work has gradually achieved wider notice and recognition. Drake signed to Island Records when he was 20 years old and released his debut album, Five Leaves Left, in 1969. By 1972, he had recorded two more albums-Bryter Layter and Pink Moon. Neither sold more than 5,000 copies on initial release. Drake's reluctance to perform live, or be interviewed, contributed to his lack of commercial success.

Drake suffered from depression and insomnia throughout his life and these topics were often reflected in his lyrics. On completion of his third album, 1972's Pink Moon, he withdrew from both live performance and recording, retreating to his parents' home in rural Warwickshire. There is no known footage of the adult Drake; he was only ever captured in still photographs and in home footage from his childhood. On 25 November 1974, Drake died from an overdose of amitriptyline, a prescribed antidepressant; he was 26 years old. Whether his death was an accident or suicide has never been resolved.

Drake's music remained available through the mid-1970s, but the 1979 release of the retrospective album Fruit Tree caused his back catalogue to be reassessed. By the mid-1980s Drake was being credited as an influence by such artists as Robert Smith, David Sylvian and Peter Buck. In 1985, The Dream Academy reached the UK and US charts with "Life in a Northern Town", a song written for and dedicated to Drake. By the early 1990s, he had come to represent a certain type of "doomed romantic" musician in the UK music press and was frequently cited as an influence by artists including Kate Bush, Paul Weller and The Black Crowes. His first biography appeared in 1997, and was followed in 1998 by the documentary film A Stranger Among Us.

perplexity.description:
The Making of Five Leaves Left" is a comprehensive four-disc retrospective documenting the creation of Nick Drake's landmark 1969 debut album. Released in July 2025 as both a 4CD and 4LP boxed set, this project compiles over 30 previously unreleased demos, studio outtakes, and alternative takes spanning from early 1968 through April 1969. The set includes Drake's first-ever session recordings from Sound Techniques studio, preserved for over fifty years on a mono listening reel by Beverley Martyn, alongside a complete reel recorded at Cambridge's Caius College by Paul de Rivaz. The final disc contains the original Joe Boyd-produced album as released in July 1969, mastered by John Wood and Simon Heywood and accompanied by a 60-page illustrated book.

The boxed set traces the meticulous evolution of Drake's arrangements and vocal interpretations across multiple recording sessions overseen by producer Joe Boyd and engineer John Wood. Tracks like "Time Has Told Me" and "River Man" appear in various incarnations, revealing how Drake and Boyd refined instrumentation—from sparse acoustic performances to orchestrated versions featuring strings, cello, and piano. "River Man," notably recorded in the unusual 5/4 time signature with a jazz feel potentially inspired by bossa nova, emerged as one of Drake's signature achievements through this iterative process.

While the original 1969 album received minimal commercial attention and radio play upon its initial release, it has since become recognized as a classic, ranking at No. 280 on Rolling Stone's 2003 list of the 500 Greatest Albums of All Time and No. 74 on NME's all-time list. The boxed set represents a definitive archival project, authorized by the Nick Drake Estate and designed to faithfully document the album's origin story rather than simply release all available takes.
